title: Reliability convergence: project plan & collaboration agenda
milestones: Mar 15 2026 - Baseline metrics and owner matrix finalized

content:
Purpose and scope:
This working plan is a cross-functional playbook to converge on a single pragmatic approach for service-level objectives (SLOs), error-budget discipline, and operational readiness across product and infra teams. It focuses on: establishing minimum observability and dashboard artifacts, clarifying SLO ownership, creating repeatable onboarding templates for feature teams, and running lightweight exercises to validate processes before an org-wide rollout.

Why now:
- Recent incidents exposed inconsistent instrumentation and fragmented ownership of customer-facing latency and availability metrics.
- Multiple product teams have bespoke SLOs with varying measurement windows and alert semantics, making escalation and prioritization hard for SRE.
- Executing a coherent SLO program will reduce incident MTTR, unify prioritization, and give product leads predictable error budgets for feature work.

Guiding principles (keep these visible in all meetings):
1) Customer-impact-first — SLOs should map to user journeys, not infra counters.
2) Minimal viable instrumentation — prefer a small set of high-signal metrics over broad but shallow telemetry.
3) Ownership clarity — every SLO has a primary product owner and an SRE co-owner.
4) Error budgets are tradeable — integrate into triage/roadmap discussions, avoid punitive framing.
5) Automate reporting and reduce manual toil.

Primary stakeholders and roles:
- Product team leads (feature owners): define customer journeys and nominate SLO PO.
- SRE (eng-sre): SLO design consultation, measurement templates, alert/playbook authors.
- Observability infra: implement dashboards, instrumentation libraries, and retention policy.
- Developer Experience: example PR templates, CI checks for metrics.
- Solutions Engineering / Support: input on customer-impact thresholds and downgrade strategies.
- Security & Compliance: ensure any telemetry changes meet PII and export controls.

Success criteria (program-level):
- 90% of feature teams have an agreed SLO and owner in the ownership matrix by May 31, 2026.
- Reduce customer-impacting incident MTTR by 30% in six months post-rollout.
- Error budget burn rate visible in weekly dashboard for top-20 services.

Concrete deliverables (short list):
- Ownership matrix CSV (service -> product-owner -> SRE co-owner)
- Template SLO definition doc (customer-journey, objective, measurement window, signal, SLI query, alert policy)
- Dashboard pack (Grafana templates): availability, p95 latency, error budget burn chart, inflight deployments with potential impact flags
- Alert templates mapped to playbooks (severity, page/no-page, runbook link)
- Onboarding checklist and 90-min training deck for feature teams
- Biweekly operational exercise plan (error-budget week, chaos-lite tests)

Example SLOs (illustrative; each service must map to the nearest customer journey):
- API: "write-requests-success-rate" SLO — Objective: 99.95% rolling 30d window. SLI: ratio of 2xx/total POST/PUT requests by customer-region. Alert: when 30d error budget burn > 25% and daily burn > 5%.
- Realtime inference edge: "p95-latency-inference" SLO — Objective: p95 < 200ms over a rolling 7d window for production traffic. SLI: p95 latency for requests with seq_len <= 1024. Alert: page if p95 > 250ms for 15m.
- Background jobs: "bulk-embeddings-completion" SLO — Objective: 99% of jobs complete within SLA window (24h). SLI: job_status=completed / jobs_started. Alert: email to owners when a backlog of >1000 jobs accumulates.

Instrumentation and measurement checklist (for each service):
- Ensure unique request IDs surface through front-to-back telemetry.
- Emit business-level success/failure counters (not only HTTP status codes).
- Record end-to-end latency (ingest->response) and relevant internal spans.
- Tag metrics with customer_tier and region where applicable.
- Export metrics to the central metrics pipeline (retention policy: 90d for raw; 365d for aggregated SLO windows).

Operational cadence and ceremonies:
- Weekly SRE x PL office hours — drop-in for SLO design questions (30m).
- Biweekly pilot team sync — review dashboards, recent burns, and open instrumentation PRs (60m).
- Monthly cross-functional review — leadership review of program health and major escalations (90m).
- Error-budget week exercises — short simulated incidents where teams practice throttling releases, switching to fallbacks, or invoking mitigation runbooks.

Pilot approach and selection criteria:
Pick 4–6 services across product and infra that: 1) represent diverse user journeys (API, console, ingestion, background), 2) have active owners who can commit ~1 engineer for 2-3 sprints, and 3) are medium risk (not critical infra that would cause company-wide outage). Pilot timeline: 6 weeks per cohort (2 weeks instrumentation & dashboard basics; 2 weeks SLO tuning & alerts; 2 weeks exercises and retros).

Rollout mechanics and tooling improvements to prioritize:
- SLO definition linter integrated with repo CI (blocks merge if SLO template missing for new services).
- Dashboards as code: Grafana/JSON template library and one-click import.
- Error budget API: lightweight service to compute and expose burn rates for dashboards and Slack bots.
- Notebook: step-by-step troubleshooting guide with queries and example dashboards.

Example runbook snippet (page 1):
- Symptom: p95 inference latency crossing threshold.
- Immediate checks (5m): check region-specific error rates, backend queue lengths, GPU utilization, and recent deploys.
- Quick mitigations (10–30m): roll back recent infra deploys, shift traffic to fallback model variant, enable reduced-batch mode, or increase autoscale policy temporarily.
- Escalation: page SRE and product owner if corrective action not effective in 30m; include recent error-budget burn and last deploys in page message.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat SLOs as additional compliance instead of a prioritization tool. Mitigation: run manager-level workshops showing concrete tradeoffs and where error budgets fund feature velocity.
- Risk: Instrumentation velocity is slow due to infra changes. Mitigation: provide turnkey libraries and pair-programming sessions with Observability infra engineers.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from poorly tuned thresholds. Mitigation: use staged alert templates (warn vs critical) and require a tuning window during pilots.

Open decisions (to discuss in next cross-functional meeting):
- Standardize measurement windows (30d vs 7d hybrid) — tradeoffs for long-window stability vs responsiveness to regressions.
- Canonical SLI set for typical services (minimal recommended signals).
- Error budget consumption visualization standards for exec reporting.

Next immediate actions (owners and due dates):
- Build initial ownership matrix draft — Owner: Marco Ruiz — due Mar 5, 2026.
- Publish SLO template and example PR — Owner: Chen Li — due Mar 8, 2026.
- Create 3 Grafana template dashboards for pilot cohort — Owner: Observability infra (Olga Petrov) — due Mar 12, 2026.
- Schedule pilot kickoff and invite pilot teams — Owner: Aisha Kaplan — due Mar 9, 2026.

Notes to reviewers (quick asks):
- Validate that example SLO objectives are aligned with product expectations for your service.
- Flag any compliance or data-export concerns from telemetry changes.
- Suggest pilot candidates by Mar 4; we will finalize cohort by Mar 6.
